title: A second fix check may start from the previous fix check's head
why: `merge --review-record` allows one Fix check line per record chain, so a second small fix (most often a main merge plus a form fix during lane lint) forces a fresh full round. On Nov 7 it hit #1679, #1670, #1439 and q_max #1106, each costing a full reviewer round for a delta with no behaviour change (coordinator, 23:29 CST). Rule roles-review-cap-three: a small fix to a round's finding gets a fix check and merges on green.
note: Fix: allow a later fix check whose base is the previous fix check's head. Not covered by open PRs: #1780 makes a failed fix check count as the next round; #1575 allows a fix base across a notes-only commit or from another PR's record (triage read both PR bodies, 23:33 CST). Stack on #1575. A queue fix under the item 384 hold. Slug from the coordinator; title by triage. 23:31 CST: lane fail-record-ancestor-head takes it as a second PR, stacked after its current one, because it owns the same fix-check code in merge.py (coordinator). The fail-record-ancestor-head lane continues here after #1795 closed (coordinator, 00:02 CST Nov 8). Ruling check (triage, 02:24 CST Nov 8): owner item 347 a (review-fix-check-round, 13:12 CST Nov 7) rules that a failed fix check counts as the next review round, inside the three-round cap; #1780 builds it. Item 356 is a different ruling (a round-3 FAIL holds). So this step follows item 347: a FAIL fix check never sends the change back to round 1. The coordinator's standing answer of 23:35 CST Nov 7 (a fresh round 1 when a chain cannot take a fix check) applies only where no failed fix check exists: a newest record that already holds a passing fix check, or a round head with no record. Clash caught by lane comment-check-scans-shell on #1834.
